title: Publish “Private deployment reference architecture” page and surface it in Security/Compliance navigation
creator: Elliot Price
project: Vertical ABM pilot: Regulated workloads (FinServ + Healthcare)
description:
Context
- ABM pilot outreach is driving regulated prospects (FinServ/Healthcare) to ask for a concrete “what does Private/VPC look like?” artifact.
- We have a strong internal reference architecture draft in Confluence, but we need a public-facing docs page that:
  1) is accurate + NDA-safe,
  2) matches current product capabilities (no roadmap promises), and
  3) is easy to find from Security/Compliance docs (where CISOs/GRC start).

Goal
Add a new docs page titled “Private deployment reference architecture” that explains (at a high level) the network boundaries and responsibility split for Redwood Private in regulated environments, and ensure it is discoverable via Security/Compliance navigation and docs search.

Scope
- Create a new page in redwood-docs under Private deployments / Architecture (final location TBD by docs IA).
- Include:
  - High-level architecture diagram (VPC boundary, control plane vs data plane, customer network, optional on-prem variant)
  - Logging/audit pipeline overview (audit events, export destinations, customer SIEM)
  - KMS/HSM integration points (where keys live; what Redwood can integrate with)
  - Responsibility matrix (Redwood vs Customer) for networking, logging, upgrades, key management, access controls
  - Clear “What this is / isn’t” disclaimer for regulated buyers (illustrative; final design varies; subject to security review)
- Navigation + discoverability:
  - Link from Security & Compliance landing/index
  - Link from Private deployments index
  - Ensure page is indexed by docs search and appears under relevant sidebar section
  - Add lightweight cross-links from related pages (audit logging, data residency/retention, SSO/RBAC) where appropriate

Out of scope (for this ticket)
- Publishing detailed step-by-step Private installation docs (separate workstream)
- Publishing customer-specific network diagrams or questionnaire evidence packs
- Any new product features (this is docs + IA)

Key stakeholders / reviewers
- Security: Dr. Aisha Rahman (final reviewer), Marcus Lin (technical accuracy), Olga Petrov (GRC phrasing)
- Solutions Engineering: Markus Klein, Simran Kaur (architecture source of truth)
- Product (Private): Vivek Kulkarni (capability/roadmap guardrails)
- Marketing/PMM: Soojin Lee (ABM alignment; ensures this matches outbound narrative)

Proposed content outline (draft)
1) Who this page is for (regulated workloads / security review prep)
2) Deployment model summary (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with focus on Private boundaries
3) Reference architecture diagram (VPC) + callouts:
   - Customer VPC (inference endpoints, routing, optional customer-managed gateway)
   - Redwood Private control plane components (management plane) vs inference runtime components (data plane)
   - Connectivity options (VPC peering / PrivateLink-equivalent language where accurate; avoid vendor-specific claims)
   - Egress controls and allowlisting considerations
4) Data flow (requests/responses), logging, and audit events
5) Key management: encryption at rest/in transit + KMS/HSM integration points (high-level)
6) Operational responsibilities (table)
7) FAQs: “Do you store prompts/outputs?”, retention knobs, audit log export, residency notes
8) Next steps CTA: “Schedule a Private/VPC technical deep dive” (routes to SE)

Acceptance criteria
- A new public docs page exists titled “Private deployment reference architecture”.
- Page includes an architecture diagram and a clear Redwood vs customer responsibility breakdown.
- Page is linked from:
  - Security/Compliance navigation (sidebar or index page)
  - Private deployments navigation
- Page content reviewed/approved by Security (Aisha + Olga) and Private product owner (Vivek).
- Page is searchable in docs site search within 24 hours of merge (or confirm indexing job ran).
- No unsupported claims re: retention/residency, certifications, or specific cloud connectivity products.

Implementation notes
- Prefer diagram format that is:
  - readable in dark mode,
  - accessible (alt text),
  - easy to update.
- If we can’t get a clean Mermaid/diagram-as-code version approved quickly, use a static SVG with source stored in repo (do not link to Google Drive).
- Ensure any “audit logging” statements match the ABM security FAQ addendum phrasing (avoid “immutable”/“WORM” claims unless explicitly true).

Risks
- Over-promising capabilities in public docs (especially around on-prem packaging maturity, retention controls, and HSM integrations).
- Diagram drifting from the actual installer architecture.

Rollout
- Merge behind normal docs deploy. No feature flag required.
- After publish: PMM to add link into ABM landing page resources section (tracked separately), and Sales/SE to use as the default “architecture overview” link for regulated discovery.
